rv.q: This drama about the 1984. Bhopal disaster is devastating when it reaches the events themselves, but is too slow to get there.
Darkling is a worthy reminder of an often-overlooked disaster – but one that may well fail to take root in the mind.
A harrowing and intriguing account of a young woman’s struggles in the face of much adversity.
The play reminds us that the world at large can be a fearsome place without itself landing the knockout emotive punch that might send us furious and fretful out into the night.
Frustrated by stunted writing, Darkling doesn’t penetrate beyond the surface level of its ideas.
There is a lot of talent, passion, and important messaging that produces lovely moments throughout this production.

Darkling perfectly captures the scale of the disaster, whilst also insisting how deeply personal its effects were.

Titas Halder's devastating new work 'Darkling', directed by Matthew Xia, brings the 1984. Bhopal disaster to the fore in this brutal and moving performance from Linnea Berthelsen.
His dense, poetic script takes us to the heart of the matter as it effects the individual and it is not a comfortable watch.
It’s searingly gruelling stuff although its unbroken 90 minute length passes quite quickly.
Halder spares us many pleasantries and gets to the human core of a simply devastating incident and, although this play does not quite convey the scale of the horror, it makes a fearless attempt.

In a show with production values this high, it really is a shame how much the writing actually lets it down.
Darkling is a show that leaves plenty for viewers to ruminate on, especially as the world continues to spiral into the climate crisis and communities continue to be destroyed by capitalistic greed.
Titas Halder and Matthew Xia have created a production that succeeds in making a huge historical event feel personal and immediate.
There is an inventiveness to the way the production transports us between places and perspectives, continually finding new ways into her world.
Darkling is an atmospheric production with an impressive central performance, however its fundamental artistic choice raises more questions than the play can answer.

cn.t: Critics praise Berthelsen's committed solo performance in this important tribute to the 1984 Bhopal disaster, though some find the 90-minute monologue slow-paced and dramatically uneven before reaching its devastating climax.
